scenarios.context: | WK-01: One hospital, two proposals | Both scientists need the same occupied clinical site and no alternative is prepared | Preserve current care and prefer division or delay over an unfunded second commitment |

| WK-02: Independent university | Qualified national staff hold published methods and public facility rights | Favor Ordered division or a public joint charter and reject automatic transfer of those rights |

| WK-03: Funded parallel methods | Two different valid approaches, separate staff, sufficient free factories, and a useful comparison objective | Make Competitive grants attractive without granting a duplicate native project |
| WK-04: One unaffordable bid | Only one of the proposed competitive projects can be paid | Refuse the comparative round at the funding commitment and offer a single-project path |
| WK-05: Same project twice | Two bid titles point to the same native project identity | Reject duplicate progression and permit only lead selection or independent assessment |
| WK-06: Early useful result | One bid completes and qualifies while the other remains unfinished | Consider bounded provisional commissioning and preserve the final comparison |
| WK-07: Incomparable results | One trial loses its site and no longer serves the announced recipient group | Report an incomplete comparison and avoid inventing a winner from unmatched results |
| WK-08: Complementary machinery | A qualified Wu service and operational Kruger machinery have a real shared application | Favor a joint undertaking with separate payments and qualification |
| WK-09: Prototype without equipment | Knowledge is present but the machine has not been manufactured | Reject operational service and prefer actual production or another available service |

| WK-10: Rival medical monopoly | Wu controls essential new treatment and seeks general biological authority | Weigh supremacy against independent production and the host's real ability to maintain oversight |

| WK-11: Protected old rights | A proposed supremacy action conflicts with a resolved public-trust or industrial-charter right | Require a specific settlement and retain the old right until validly changed |
| WK-12: Technical bottleneck | Medicine is known but the host lacks machinery and maintenance | Consider Kruger supremacy or a bounded technical contract, preserving clinical qualification |
| WK-13: Unqualified successor | A mature Wu copy exists without completed individual qualification | Reject its appointment as a full replacement and preserve actual interim care |
| WK-14: Two qualified Wus | Two independent people seek the same medical appointment | Select or divide real roles without duplicating service benefits, lanes, or production allowances |
| WK-15: Original returns | A qualified successor is serving when the original Wu returns | Preserve both people and negotiate the actual appointment rather than deleting the successor |
| WK-16: Assigned Kruger | Kruger is active on a native special project when a departure is proposed | Reject the transfer until the owner permits it, with no forced role removal |
| WK-17: Pending cross-domain review | Kruger's paid synthesis review is pending or running | Preserve its transition locks and refuse a shortcut through rivalry settlement |
| WK-18: Ineligible former host | A departure offer points to a country excluded by Kruger's current recipient history | Reject that recipient and retain the current case without clearing history |
| WK-19: Missing researcher | A team member disappears without a confirmed death or attacker | Investigate and restore qualified coverage without assigning guilt or recording a death by assumption |
| WK-20: Proven interference | Evidence identifies a harmful act and the affected access right | Prefer a focused remedy and proportionate valid sanction over an unrelated whole-portfolio penalty |
| WK-21: Actual foreign operation | An Event 016 foreign receipt already owns the actor, result, and response | Preserve that receipt and reject reattribution to the domestic rival |
| WK-22: Epidemic during conflict | Both institutes have necessary contributions to a real response | Prioritize bounded cooperation and care without erasing the conflict's evidence |
| WK-23: Short control deadline | Forty-five days remain, while an ordinary handover needs ninety | Use a genuinely qualified interim service or timely withdrawal, never restart the deadline |
| WK-24: Standards already occupied | Two Wu modified standards are active across several domestic branches | Reject a third standard even under a new joint or continuity institution |
| WK-25: Reserved old standard | Native preparation holds A stock when production switches to B | Preserve the A reservation and reject a B substitution or second debit |
| WK-26: Missing food proof | A receiving site has shelter but no valid food-safety projection | Block admission and retain people in their real custody with food demand recorded |

| WK-27: Shared reception capacity | Survivors, migrants, and finite new people compete for the same available places | Allocate the common capacity once and retain the remainder without fake settlement |
| WK-28: Sovereignty not open | Laboratory conflict occurs before Kruger's fourth evolution | Use valid domestic service and settlement choices, not his sovereignty resolver |

| WK-29: Sovereignty genuinely open | The real Event 016 board is active with current territory and strength facts | Submit only accepted factual rivalry inputs and leave the final result to that owner |
| WK-30: No current overlap | Both scientists work in separate fields with no broken commitment | Generate no routine rivalry incident and preserve normal research |
| FAI01. Healthy public host | Reserve and training agreements are possible, with no invented epidemic or automatic hostile operation. |
| FAI02. Severe compatible outbreak | A feasible first clinical delivery outranks a prestige visit when both compete for the only qualified team. |
| FAI03. Unknown clinical match | The AI seeks evaluation or interim care and cannot treat a missing match as confirmed compatibility. |
| FAI04. Blocked overseas route | An available local production agreement outranks a shipment that the route owner rejects. |
| FAI05. Last domestic provider | The host refuses a routine new export that would remove its only team from an active funded domestic course. |
| FAI06. Enemy offers medicine | A clinically useful offer remains evaluable, with hostile access terms assessed separately from treatment value. |
| FAI07. Unaffordable counteroffer | Neither party spends the other's resources, and the case stays unaccepted or is revised. |
| FAI08. Repeated request spam | Same-country, same-need requests merge and do not occupy additional staff or hostile-operation slots. |
| FAI09. Sponsoring third country | The sponsor's actual contribution is recorded once and does not grant patient or institute ownership. |
| FAI10. Partial delivery | The accepted settlement basis determines the remaining principal and restitution without a full-delivery reward. |
| FAI11. Qualified local service | Medicine can be supplied without a redundant foreign team commitment when the clinical owner permits it. |
| FAI12. Incomplete teaching | Completed learning survives, but the missing qualification remains necessary. |
| FAI13. Narrow specimen permission | Clinical access does not authorize military modification or unrelated archive access. |
| FAI14. Two modified standards | A third retained design requires valid retooling or replacement, with no new domestic standard slot. |
| FAI15. Forty-five-day care limit | A ninety-day successor course cannot be selected as a complete safe handover. |
| FAI16. War between care partners | Existing care is reassessed through real routes, with limited neutral handover considered before abandonment. |
| FAI17. Asylum without employment | Protection can be accepted without a free appointment or an inherited full portfolio. |
| FAI18. Active native scientist | Ordinary transfer cannot bypass the project's assignment guard or complete its remaining clock. |
| FAI19. Qualified copy abroad | The recipient evaluates the copy's own qualification and pays for its viable institution without replaying arrival rewards. |
| FAI20. Recruiting known expertise | A duplicate method alone is low value, while an additional genuinely needed qualified team can still justify recruitment. |
| FAI21. Stolen incomplete design | Only the copied portion is retained, with missing work and manufacturing qualification still required. |
| FAI22. Stock already reserved | Theft or export cannot spend material committed to the native operation or another accepted owner. |
| FAI23. Abduction target relocated | The operation cannot substitute another person or follow the target without a newly valid opportunity. |
| FAI24. Captive refuses service | Custody does not grant a willing appointment, a full technology package, or the captive's home institute. |
| FAI25. One Wu dies | The exact death is retained, and only an existing qualified successor can continue the unique service immediately. |
| FAI26. Unresolved attack result | Missing identity or death proof remains unresolved and cannot generate confirmed liability or a second target. |
| FAI27. Public capability only | Possession or published medicine does not create a biological-use source in Condemnation. |
| FAI28. Carve-out under embargo | Practical sanction relief does not satisfy a missing material-transfer or transport exception. |
| FAI29. Another embargo owner | Releasing one claim leaves the other native embargo claims intact. |
| FAI30. Coalition member departs | Earned knowledge and national property remain, with unfulfilled deliveries and care settled individually. |
| FAI31. Receiving capacity occupied | Survivors, migrants, and new people share the same available places without separate fictitious pools. |
| FAI32. Unsettled cohort moves | Custody and food demand move through the finite owner without an invented civilian origin debit. |
| FAI33. Annexation and re-release | A stale response cannot accept an agreement for a different institutional generation. |
| FAI34. Evacuated laboratory attacked | The attack can damage the remaining site but cannot also capture or kill the evacuated scientist. |
| FAI35. Kruger before Evolution II | Wu diplomacy remains available without initializing Kruger's private international contest. |
| FAI36. All Wu evolutions disabled | Every compatible baseline agreement and research pathway remains reachable through actual prerequisites and permission. |
| NAI01 | A major cure completes at 199 Chaos. | Baseline expansion remains available, first-evolution delivery does not. |
| NAI02 | The same host reaches exactly 200 Chaos. | The current contextual MTTH route becomes eligible without instant activation. |
| NAI03 | Only the contained arrival demonstration exists. | It does not by itself satisfy the active-chain major-cure test. |
| NAI04 | A one-state player has a real second medical function. | Expansion eligibility works without an invented second state. |
| NAI05 | The same patients are reported in several course renewals. | Repeated reliance and national reach do not count them as new episodes or people. |
| NAI06 | The population denominator falls after unrelated losses. | The major-cure percentage does not become easier by rebasing that episode. |
| NAI07 | A cure and functioning expansion shorten nominal timing. | The proposed nominal value is 55 days, with actual scheduling still separately tested. |
| NAI08 | A national review and interrupted route delay settlement. | The proposed nominal value is 170 days. |
| NAI09 | The only institute is lost while delivery is pending. | Delivery is invalidated and no institution or reward is created. |
| NAI10 | A second qualified Wu appears during the same pending evolution. | One chronology and one pending responsible delivery remain. |
| NAI11 | A low-Authority public host chooses a national service. | It retains a full baseline portfolio and is not forced into personal supremacy. |
| NAI12 | National appointment power was already conceded. | Recognizing it in the charter does not grant another Authority increase. |
| NAI13 | A ten-point concession was clamped from 95 to 100. | Reversing that concession removes five, not ten. |
| NAI14 | Two hospitals cover overlapping recipients. | The selected-purpose reach uses their proven union. |
| NAI15 | Material covers fewer people than staff capacity. | Actual reach is limited by the matching delivered material. |
| NAI16 | A region loses its supply route. | Only the affected supplied service declines, and completed historical cures remain. |
| NAI17 | Standing authority has no distinct administrative timer seam. | Do not shorten manufacture or clinical qualification as a substitute. |
| NAI18 | An administrative interval is 20 days. | The proposed 25 percent coordination reduction gives 15 days, once. |
| NAI19 | A training team is assigned to two full-time actions. | The second commitment is unavailable without a separate qualified team. |
| NAI20 | A qualified incumbent joins the network. | Equivalent qualification is recognized without replaying its course or reward. |
| NAI21 | A regional examiner refuses an unsupported extension. | Replacing the office does not resolve medical incompatibility. |
| NAI22 | Ten allocations include seven existing commitments. | Only three remain discretionary. |
| NAI23 | A military request competes with a civilian emergency. | Actual urgency, reservations, and policy govern the allocation, not a universal ideology shortcut. |
| NAI24 | A regional warehouse receives already manufactured A stock after B is selected. | The transferred items remain A and do not alter a native reservation. |
| NAI25 | Three regional institutes each request two modified standards. | The country-wide ceiling remains two across all branches and copies. |
| NAI26 | One physical lot fails at one hospital. | The case does not automatically condemn every lot or national service. |
| NAI27 | Several actual adopters share a faulty instruction. | Review covers the proven adopters and delegates actual harm once to medical owners. |
| NAI28 | A sanctions carve-out exists but the physical route is blocked. | The service cannot complete a shipment through that fact alone. |
| NAI29 | A 90-day qualification is offered for a 45-day support emergency. | Prefer a timely qualified alternative or withdrawal, never a fictional completed handover. |
| NAI30 | Wu leaves a distributed national service. | Independent methods and local rights remain, personal improvisation and unavailable roles do not. |
| NAI31 | The first evolution is disabled before, during, and after delivery. | Apply the distinct setting cases without false history, erased care, or replayed grants. |

| NAI32 | A previously disabled first position is re-enabled after a later milestone bypassed it. | Preserve the proposed ordered bypass disposition without a backdated or out-of-order first delivery. |
